goal: how to add an email draft
preamble: An email draft in Docs isn't a note reminding you to write an email later. It's a small structured block — To, Subject, body — that Docs knows how to hand off to Gmail when you're done. So you're not typing an email into a document; you're placing a piece of scaffolding that Gmail will later recognise. That distinction is why you won't find it anywhere in the formatting tools.
generalization: Building blocks are the pattern worth keeping: Docs has a handful of pre-shaped chunks — email drafts, meeting notes, product roadmaps — that carry structure Docs itself understands. Anything you could type by hand but Docs offers ready-made is usually a building block, and that means it does something extra once it's there. The email draft's Gmail button only exists because you inserted a block rather than typing three lines of text.

steps.intent: Nothing here is being formatted or edited — you're putting something into the document that wasn't there before. That's one menu's entire job, and it's the same menu you'd use for a table, an image, or a page break.
hints: You're adding, not changing. Which menu is about things that don't exist in the document yet?
The Insert menu, in the menu bar along the top.

wrongHints.Format: Format changes text that already exists — bold, spacing, alignment. There's nothing here yet to format.
wrongHints.File: File is about the document as a whole: sharing, printing, history. The email draft goes inside the document, not around it.

steps.intent: The Insert menu is long, and most of it is single pieces — an image, a link, a line. An email draft is none of those; it's a ready-made arrangement of several fields at once. Docs keeps that whole category together under one name.
hints: You're not inserting one thing, you're inserting a small pre-built structure. Docs has a group for exactly that.
'Building blocks', in the upper half of the Insert menu, with an arrow showing a submenu.

wrongHints.Table: A table would give you rows and boxes, and you could arrange To and Subject inside one. But it would only ever be a table — Docs wouldn't know it was an email.

steps.intent: Your turn, no highlight. The submenu that opened is a short list of the block types Docs knows how to build. Pick the one that matches what you actually want, and watch what appears — it won't be plain text, it will be a block with its own fields and a Gmail button at the edge.
hints: Only one of these building blocks is about correspondence rather than project planning.
Near the top of the submenu that just opened to the right.

wrongHints.Meeting notes: Also a building block, and also pre-structured — but it fills itself from a calendar event. The email draft is the one that connects to Gmail.
